Gabriel, appearing as a stranger, asked the Prophet about Islam, faith, excellence and the signs of the Hour; Ibn Umar cited it against those denying Divine Decree.
Men asking what Allah requires were told prayer, Ramadan's fast, Zakat and Hajj, with Paradise if true to it, and Islam is built on five pillars.
The Abdul Qais delegation was commanded faith in Allah, explained as the testimony, prayer, Zakat, fasting and a fifth of booty, and forbidden four kinds of drinking vessels.
Sending Mu'adh to People of the Book in Yemen, the Prophet told him to call them first to the testimony, then prayer, then Zakat, without taking their best property.
The Prophet was commanded to fight people until they testify there is no god but Allah, which protects their blood and property; Abu Bakr resolved to fight those withholding Zakat.
Dying, Abu Talib refused the Prophet's plea to profess there is no god but Allah, and verses came on not seeking forgiveness for polytheists and Allah guiding whom He wills.
Whoever dies knowing there is no god but Allah, and meets Him without doubt of this and of the Prophet's mission, enters Paradise and is barred from Hell.
Allah's right is that servants worship without partners, and theirs that He not punish them; the news was withheld lest people rely on it, and the testimony saves from Hell.
One content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion and Muhammad as Prophet tastes faith, which has over sixty or seventy branches, modesty among them.
Modesty is part of faith and brings nothing but good; Imran grew angry when Bushair set books of wisdom against the Prophet's words on it.
Asked for a word on Islam that would need no other, the Prophet said to affirm faith in Allah and then remain steadfast.
The best in Islam is feeding people and greeting those one knows and does not know, and the best Muslim is he from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe.
Faith's sweetness comes from loving Allah and His Messenger above all, loving for Allah's sake and hating return to unbelief; none believes until the Prophet is dearest to him.
None truly believes until he loves for his brother, or his neighbour, what he loves for himself.
No one whose neighbour is unsafe from him enters Paradise; a believer treats his neighbour well, honours his guest, and speaks good or keeps silent.
Evil should be changed by hand, else tongue, else in the heart, the least of faith, and whoever strives so against those who forsake a prophet's way is a believer.
Faith, understanding and tender hearts are with the people of Yemen, and faith with the Hijaz, while unbelief and harshness lie east, pride among camel owners, calm among shepherds.
None enters Paradise without faith or has faith without loving one another, and spreading the greeting of peace fosters that love.
Religion is sincerity to Allah, His Book, His Messenger and the Muslims' leaders and people; Jarir pledged prayer, Zakat, hearing and obeying, and goodwill to every Muslim.
No one is a believer while he commits fornication, theft, drinking wine or plunder, and repentance may be accepted afterwards.
Lying, breaking promises, betraying trust and abusive disputing are signs of a hypocrite, even one who fasts, prays and claims to be Muslim; having one is a trait of hypocrisy.
Calling a Muslim an unbeliever returns to one of the two; knowingly claiming another man as one's father is unbelief, and claiming what is not one's own earns the Fire.
Detesting one's father is unbelief, and Paradise is forbidden to whoever knowingly claims a man other than his real father as his father.
Abusing a Muslim is an outrage and fighting him is unbelief; at the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet warned not to turn unbelievers after him by striking one another's necks.
Slandering lineage and wailing over the dead are akin to unbelief, and a slave who flees his master commits unbelief, loses protection and has his prayer refused.
After rain, those crediting Allah's mercy believe in Him while those crediting a star disbelieve in Him, and the verse on the setting of the stars came about this.
Loving the Ansar is a sign of faith and hating them a sign of hypocrisy; no believer in Allah and the Last Day bears them a grudge.
Ali swore the Prophet promised him that only a believer would love him and only a hypocrite would bear him a grudge.
The Prophet told women to give charity and seek forgiveness, having seen many women in Hell for cursing and ingratitude to husbands, and named a lack in sense and religion.
When a person prostrates at a verse of prostration, Satan withdraws weeping that man obeyed and earned Paradise while he refused and is doomed to Hell.
Between a man and polytheism and unbelief stands the abandoning of prayer.
The best deeds are faith in Allah, jihad and an accepted Hajj, or prayer on time, kindness to parents and jihad; the costliest slave is best to free.
The gravest sins include associating partners with Allah, killing one's child, adultery with a neighbour's wife, disobeying or abusing parents, false testimony, and the seven destructive sins.
